definitions.explanation: A person who attacks and robs ships at sea. Also used for historical pirates and in modern contexts such as pirated goods ({海賊版|かいぞくばん}).

examples.japanese: {海賊|かいぞく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧。
⟦かつて→かつて：10303_katsute⟧⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{海域|かいいき}→海域：26897_kaiiki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{海賊|かいぞく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}かった→多い：01127_ooi⟧。

notes:
USAGE:
The compound ⟦{海賊版|かいぞくばん}→海賊版：21234_kaizokuban⟧ (pirated edition/version) is very common in modern Japanese, referring to unauthorized copies of software, movies, books, and other media.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japan has its own history of piracy. The {倭寇|わこう} were pirates who raided the coasts of China and Korea from the 13th to 16th centuries. {村上水軍|むらかみすいぐん} (Murakami naval forces) controlled the Seto Inland Sea during the medieval period. In popular culture, pirates feature prominently in manga and anime.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{海賊版|かいぞくばん}→海賊版：21234_kaizokuban⟧: pirated edition, bootleg
- {海賊|かいぞく}{船|せん}: pirate ship
- {海賊|かいぞく}⟦{行為|こうい}→行為：10021_koui⟧: piracy
- {海賊|かいぞく}{旗|はた}: pirate flag, Jolly Roger
